gaps.sentence: The film didn't live up ___ my expectations.
gaps.explanation: live up TO something = be as good as expected.

gaps.sentence: The protesters set ___ at dawn from the village square.
gaps.explanation: set off/out = begin a journey; set up = establish.

gaps.sentence: The ministry tried to play ___ the incident.
gaps.explanation: play down = make something seem less important (opposite: play up).

gaps.sentence: They set ___ to climb the north face in April.
gaps.explanation: set out (to do) = begin a job/mission with a goal.

gaps.sentence: He ___ up the word in an online dictionary.
gaps.explanation: 'Look a word up' = check its meaning.
run out OF something = have none left.

gaps.sentence: Hurry ___ or we'll miss the ferry!
Don't ___ up all the milk — we need some for breakfast.
gaps.explanation: use up = finish the whole supply of something.
